data.summary: Dia::Core::JobSystem (Dia/DiaCore/Threading/JobSystem.h) is a header-only Meyers-singleton wrapping a ThreadPool, exposing Job*/CreateJob/Run/Wait + parent-child + ParallelFor. Production callers (TextureHandler, AsyncFileLoader, JobSystemModule) only use Create/Run/Wait. The implementation has correctness bugs (child-job leaks, no-op work-stealing, unguarded double-Run), unimplemented advertised features (priorities, work stealing), and confused ownership (singleton + module wrapper).
strengths: Single small header — easy to replace wholesale
JobSystemModule already owns init/shutdown lifecycle on MainPU (per spec jobsystem-module.md)
Atomic.h, Mutex.h, Thread.h primitives are clean and reusable
Existing GoogleTest suite covers basic Submit/Wait/parent-child/ParallelFor — useful as a regression net even if some tests will be retired

debt.title: Child jobs leak unconditionally
debt.evidence: JobSystem.h:166-178 — WaitImpl only DIA_DELETEs the job it was called on. CreateChildJob allocations are never freed.
debt.impact: Every ParallelFor leaks N Job + std::function allocations.

debt.title: Wait() can deadlock if invoked from inside a running job
debt.evidence: JobSystem.h:166-173 — spin/yield loop never executes pending tasks. Comment 'Could implement work stealing here' confirms feature is missing.
debt.impact: Header advertises work stealing (line 33) that doesn't exist; nested job patterns can stall.

debt.title: ThreadPool::Shutdown drops queued tasks
debt.evidence: ThreadPool.h:94-110 — sets shutdown flag and joins; never drains queue. Job allocations enqueued but not run leak.
debt.impact: App shutdown leaks Jobs + lambdas; no diagnostic for unfinished work.

debt.title: Run() is not idempotent and unguarded
debt.evidence: JobSystem.h:157-164 — calling Run twice enqueues two copies; second Finish underflows unfinishedJobs and races with Wait's DIA_DELETE.
debt.impact: Silent corruption + use-after-free on misuse; no assert.

debt.title: Job lifetime contract is undocumented and unenforceable
debt.evidence: JobSystem.h:99-103, 177 — IsComplete reads job->unfinishedJobs which is freed in Wait. Caller can UAF; second Wait will double-delete.
debt.impact: API forces callers to track job liveness manually; TextureHandler works around with shared_ptr.

debt.title: Initialize/Shutdown not thread-safe and silently no-op on re-init
debt.evidence: JobSystem.h:121-136 — `if (!mThreadPool) ...` not guarded; second concurrent Initialize races. Re-init after Shutdown silently rebuilds.
debt.impact: Module lifecycle owns this in practice, but the API permits misuse.

debt.title: Singleton dtor performs Shutdown at process exit
debt.evidence: JobSystem.h:110-113 — ~JobSystem() calls ShutdownImpl. Runs after JobSystemModule::DoStop already shut down (or didn't).
debt.impact: Two shutdown paths; ordering depends on static destruction (undefined relative to other globals).

debt.title: Two std::function layers per submission
debt.evidence: Job::function (std::function<void(Job*)>) is captured into a ThreadPool::Task (std::function<void()>).
debt.impact: Two heap allocations + two indirect calls per non-SBO lambda; matters for ParallelFor hot paths.

debt.title: Job is heap-allocated per submission
debt.impact: 1000-item ParallelFor = 1000 Jobs + 1000 lambda captures + 1000 mutex pushes. No pool.

debt.title: priority field exists but ThreadPool ignores it
debt.evidence: JobSystem.h:48 declares priority; ThreadPool.h:166 uses std::queue<Task> (FIFO).

debt.title: All implementation lives in headers
debt.impact: Touching either recompiles every TU that includes them.

debt.title: Singleton + module wrapper is a confused ownership contract
debt.evidence: JobSystemModule (Cluiche/CluicheGameBaseline/Modules/JobSystemModule.cpp) calls JobSystem::Initialize/Shutdown — but JobSystem is a global. The module owns lifecycle but not the instance.
debt.impact: Cannot have two instances (e.g., for tests); cannot inject a stub; dependency invisible to callers.

debt.title: Header docstring advertises features not implemented

duplication.title: Two 'wait' semantics across the layer
duplication.evidence: ThreadPool::WaitAll waits for queue drain; JobSystem::Wait waits for one job tree. Subtle overlap; AsyncFileLoader uses both.

duplication.title: Two thread abstractions
duplication.evidence: Dia::Core::Thread (with name + priority slot) exists, but ThreadPool uses raw std::thread.

hidden_coupling.title: Callers must externally keep job-captured state alive
hidden_coupling.evidence: TextureHandler.cpp:101-114 wraps PendingUpload in shared_ptr because the Job::function lambda captures it; the Job itself does not retain its own lambda after Finish runs.
hidden_coupling.impact: Every async caller must learn this dance.

hidden_coupling.title: Caller must drain its own outstanding jobs before JobSystemModule::DoStop
hidden_coupling.evidence: Per jobsystem-module.md AI Q2: AssetService stops first and must Wait on outstanding jobs; if any caller forgets, Shutdown can hang or leak.
hidden_coupling.impact: Module-graph dependency carries an unwritten 'drain on stop' contract.

hidden_coupling.title: JobSystemModule.cpp depends on JobSystem header pulling in ThreadPool transitively
hidden_coupling.evidence: JobSystemModule.cpp includes only JobSystem.h; ThreadPool/Atomic come along.
hidden_coupling.impact: Header-only design means any change to ThreadPool internals reaches the module's TU.

missing_tests: No test for double-Run (currently silent corruption)
No test for Wait()-from-inside-job (the deadlock scenario)
No assert/diagnostic when Submit is called after Shutdown
No test that proves child-job storage is freed (would catch the leak)
No test that verifies a worker can outlive a re-Init/Shutdown cycle cleanly
likely_invariants: Submit(fn) eventually calls fn() exactly once on a worker thread
Wait(handle) returns only after fn() has fully executed
After Wait returns, the handle and any captured lambda state can be released safely
Shutdown completes only after all submitted-and-not-yet-completed work is finished or cancelled (current pick: finished)
Submit after Shutdown is a programmer error (assert)
Re-init after Shutdown produces a fresh, independent worker pool
Concurrent Submit from many threads is safe
Wait is safe to call from any thread, including a worker thread (within the same instance) — must not deadlock when caller is on a worker
recommended_cleanup_order: 1. Decide ownership model: drop singleton, JobSystem becomes a value type owned by JobSystemModule. Service-locator or pointer-handed-to-callers.
2. Collapse API to three primitives — Submit / Wait / IsComplete — returning a refcounted JobHandle that owns Job storage. Eliminates manual delete and double-Run hazard.
3. Move impl out of header to JobSystem.cpp / ThreadPool.cpp (PIMPL or just .cpp).
4. Strip dead/misleading surface: remove priority field, remove work-stealing comment, remove ParallelFor + parent-child until needed.
5. Tighten ThreadPool shutdown: drain or assert-on-pending; document semantic.
6. Add diagnostics: assert Submit-after-Shutdown; assert Wait on stale handle is safe (refcount handles it).
7. Add the missing tests listed above.
8. Update tests to drop parent/child + ParallelFor cases; keep core Submit/Wait coverage.
9. Update TextureHandler and AsyncFileLoader to use new handle-based API; verify no behavior regression.
